<reason>CON won a close, high-quality clash by keeping the motion on a comparative instrument test: whether a common coal clock beats binding emissions pathways plus finance. PRO had a coherent political-economy story about residual plants and neighbor-delay, but CON repeatedly showed that climate success is cumulative emissions and replacement quality, then used PRO’s own concessions on short extensions and coal-to-gas compliance to argue the clock either stops being common or rewards a worse outcome. PRO never established the extra climate value of synchronized retirement over enforceable reductions.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s second rebuttal after the pressure questions: PRO’s “short verified extension” and admission that long-lived gas could satisfy the coal obligation turned the common timeline into either dissolving dates or a rush into an inferior substitute.</best_rebuttal>
